newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 22.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Thursday.

- Attempts will be made next week to revive the stalled political talks process in Northern Ireland despite the setback represented by Thursday's thwarted car-bomb attack in Derry for which responsibility was claimed by the IRA Continuity Army Council.
- The minister for Transport has urged the National Bus and Rail Union to use the state's industrial relations machinery to avert a national transport strike next month.
- Rynair, the privately-owned Irish airline, has launched a strong attack on Aer Rianta's landing charges.
- A new law imposing a 48-hour working week will have no effect on the competetiveness of Irish companies, Minister of State for Labour Affairs, Eithne Fitzgeral said on Thursday.
- A crucial meeting has been called by the coalition leaders on Sunday to thrash out government spending and tax plans for next year.

- Police in Northern Ireland have ordered tighter security at shopping centres in the run-up to Christmas following the discovery of a large bomb planted by a breakaway IRA group in Derry on Thursday.
- Strong lending and a low bad debt pushed National Irish Bank's profits to record levels for the year ended September last.
